tier_reason: bbi-js docs/wasm.md prints wasm-vs-pako timings from the public harness benchmarks/inflate.bench.ts, and the Rust release profile is public in crate/Cargo.toml, but neither the CPU model nor the Node version is stated, and the numbers are first-party (same author), so the tier stays C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: bbi-js docs/wasm.md (benchmarks/inflate.bench.ts, best of three runs, mean ms): wasm 1.9 ms vs pako 6.0 ms on volvox.bw (49 blocks), 5.4 vs 16.6 ms on cow.bw (125), 31 vs 86 ms on ENCFF826FLP.bw (436), 29 vs 62 ms on variable_step_large.bw (489), i.e. 2.1-3.2x (derived from page data). The doc's own speedup table gives per-fixture ranges of 2.3-3.8x across three runs and summarizes them as '~2.5-3x faster'. The platform DecompressionStream, called once per block, is 4-11x slower than wasm. The inflate-js README's 'roughly 4x faster than pako' is not backed by any table and exceeds the doc's own summary.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Rust crate (libdeflater 1.x with the freestanding feature, so libdeflate's C is built through cc-rs by a wasm-capable clang) built with cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown. The release profile in crate/Cargo.toml sets opt-level=3, lto=true, codegen-units=1 and panic=abort. wasm-bindgen runs at the Cargo.lock version, webpack base64-inlines the result, and there is no wasm-opt pass. The Node version is not stated. Baseline pako is ^3.0.1 per bbi-js package.json.
corrections.baseline: pako 3.x inflateRaw (pure JavaScript inflate in V8), called once per block with a chunkSize hint. Both arms skip the 2-byte zlib header and leave adler32 unchecked.
corrections.caveats: The benchmark lives in the sibling repo bbi-js (benchmarks/inflate.bench.ts, MIT, same author) and runs bbi-js's copy of the crate. Its inflate_raw_batch matches inflate-js's except for the bounds and length checks inflate-js added. inflate-js has no benchmark of its own; it is a 5-commit extraction (v1.0.0, August 2026). The harness asserts byte-identical output before timing, and both arms skip the zlib header and the adler32 check, so the comparison does equal work. CPU, Node version and run count beyond 'three runs on one machine' are not stated, and the doc asks readers to 'treat them as an order of magnitude'. The README's '4x' overstates the doc's 2.5-3x summary. The win is inflate in isolation: an older end-to-end whole-genome parseBigWig comparison was only about 5% apart. Raw deflate has no checksum, so corrupt but legal streams decode silently.

notes: Real entry with a fair, byte-checked harness. Shortcomings to record: the README's 4x claim exceeds the bbi-js doc's 2.5-3x (derived 2.1-3.2x); CPU and Node version are unstated; the benchmark is in bbi-js, not in inflate-js; and the end-to-end gain is about 5%. tier_reason: The README table comes from the public bench/bench.mjs, and docs/comparison.md from bench/compare/run.mjs. Release flags are public in Cargo.toml, but the hardware is only 'macOS arm64' with no CPU model, so these first-party numbers are tier C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README table (bench/bench.mjs; every ratio is against SheetJS read + sheet_to_json). Large 1.8M-cell 23 MB sheet: toCsv 865 ms (5.3x), readCells values 981 ms (4.7x) and readCells tagged 1.53 s (3.0x) vs SheetJS sheet_to_json 4.61 s (sheet_to_csv 4.57 s). Medium 400k cells: toCsv 188 ms and readCells values 190 ms vs sheet_to_json 786 ms (4.2x and 4.1x, derived from page data). Small 5k cells: toCsv 2 ms vs sheet_to_csv 8 ms (4x, derived from page data) and readCells values 3 ms vs sheet_to_json 8 ms (2.7x, derived from page data). docs/comparison.md (one subprocess per library, bench/compare/run.mjs) gives readCellsParsed ~1.0 s vs SheetJS read + sheet_to_json ~4.0 s on the large file, about 4x.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: wasm-pack build --release --target web (scripts/build.mjs). The Cargo release profile sets opt-level=3, lto=true, codegen-units=1 and panic=abort. Rust is pinned in rust-toolchain.toml, and wasm-opt comes from binaryen 131+. Runs used Node 22.18, with Bun 1.3.5 also run. The README table comes from bench/bench.mjs (bun run bench), the comparison.md cost table from bench/compare/run.mjs.
corrections.hardware: macOS arm64 (CPU model not stated); comparison.md run dated 2026-08-10
corrections.workload: Reading synthetic .xlsx fixtures generated by bench/make-fixtures.mjs, which writes them with SheetJS: a type mix of strings, numbers, dates, booleans and holes. Sizes are small 500x10 (5k cells), medium 20,000x20 (400k cells) and large 150,000x12 (1.8M cells, 23 MB). Each run converts the first sheet to CSV or cell arrays and reports the median of 20, 5 and 3 iterations respectively, on Node 22.18.
corrections.caveats: Author-run benchmark. The scripts are public, but the fixtures are generated (not committed) by bench/make-fixtures.mjs, and the CPU model is not stated. bench/bench.mjs runs every strategy in one process in sequence, wasm first. The large file gets only 3 iterations (median, first iteration included), and every speedup divides by SheetJS sheet_to_json, even for the CSV rows. The README says 'up to 5x' while the large-file tables show 3.0-5.3x, and comparison.md itself says 'about 4x'. The SheetJS baseline is the npm-frozen xlsx 0.18.5, not the maintained CDN releases. comparison.md is candid that SheetJS has wider format coverage and maturity, and that the speed comes partly from doing less (read-only, four formats). This is an unofficial binding of tafia/calamine, so the parsing speed is calamine's. The repo has 27 commits, at version 0.1.0 with one maintainer, and wasm32 caps it at 4 GB.

notes: Numbers match the README. The record's medium ratio compares toCsv against sheet_to_json, which is the harness's own convention; I added the matching readCells figure. Shortcomings: no CPU model; few iterations in one shared process; the baseline is the npm-frozen SheetJS 0.18.5; fixtures are synthetic; 'up to 5x' vs 'about 4x' in its own comparison doc. tier_reason: The README numbers come from the public bench/index.mjs, and the build flags are public (wasi-sdk 21.0 clang -Oz, binaryen 116 wasm-opt -Oz). But no CPU or Node version is stated and the numbers are first-party, so the tier is C.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: wasi-sdk 21.0 clang -target wasm32-unknown-wasi -Oz (build/Makefile), then binaryen 116 wasm-opt -Oz; versions are pinned in build/wasm.js and built via docker or npm run build-wasm-local. The build optimises for size, not speed. The JS build is lexer.js. The Node version is not stated; the README numbers date from November 2020, the Node 14 era.
corrections.caveats: First-party README numbers with no CPU or Node version, run with npm run bench (bench/index.mjs). git blame dates the benchmark block to the 2020-11-02 commit d38263b and the '1.5x faster' line to 2020-09-27. They predate the wasi-sdk/binaryen builder change (2024) and the September-October 2026 perf commits (#122, #123, #124, #131), so they are about six years stale. The harness rounds every timed parse to whole milliseconds (Math.round per call) before averaging, so per-file warm figures under a few ms (magic-string 0.64/0.16/0 ms) are rounding artifacts and the all-samples sums carry up to about 4 ms of rounding per run. The baseline is the project's own JavaScript build, not a third-party package. The warm-run advantage is only 1.45x; the 6.95x cold-run gap reflects JIT warm-up of the JS build that the Wasm build skips. Wasm module load is slower (10 ms vs 4 ms).

notes: Numbers match the README exactly (cold 299 vs 43 ms, warm 40.28 vs 27.76 ms, load 4 vs 10 ms). Shortcomings to record: the numbers are from November 2020 and stale relative to the 2026 perf commits; there is no hardware or Node version; the harness has whole-millisecond rounding; the baseline is the project's own JS build.
